note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Trace the entire fibrous-rooted cool-season annual (often 2–30 cm) to its short ~1–8 cm terminal head. Nearly straight rigid, angular branches carry tightly appressed oblong spikelets, often looking like miniature one-sided fern combs. The current archived whole-plant photograph supports the silhouette, not the branch cross-section or microscopic anatomy.
tiles.short: Tiny annual; stiff green fern-comb flowering head
tiles.status: FIELD-READY GROSS CUE; NEEDS MEASURED ATTACHED PLANT

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1260) — Open the inner leaf junction for the membranous ligule. Under Desmazeria rigida, the Flora gives 1.5–4 mm.

Panels 2–3 are source-labelled Catapodium collar photographs. Panel 3 (zero-based index 2), Stefan.lefnaer's archived CC BY-SA 4.0 macro, was actually pixel-inspected: translucent collar membrane tissue and the photographer's printed 2-mm scale are visible, with two existing arrows onto those visible features. The free ligule apex and a defensible 1–3 mm membrane length are NOT resolved. Panel 2 (index 1) still needs pixel inspection. Open a fresh inner blade–sheath junction, expose the free membrane edge and measure it beside 1-mm graduations; do not equate nearby hairs with ligule length.
tiles.short: Blunt membranous ligule: source photo shows real membrane tissue and a 2-mm scale
tiles.status: ACTUAL COLLAR TISSUE + PRINTED SCALE PHOTOGRAPHED — FREE APEX/LENGTH UNVERIFIED

tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW THE SHORT PEDICEL
tiles.details: NEW real photographer-scale sl17 at gallery panel 6 (index5) shows TWO views of actual tight upright narrow panicle and attached MULTI-FLORET spikelets, with a 20mm scale. Photographer's sl26 (index6) directly labels lower/upper glumes and several fertile lemmas inside one spikelet at 5mm. The three-angled rachis cross-section and precise 0.5–1.5mm pedicel attachment remain unverified; don't infer them from broad two-face photograph.
tiles.status: ACTUAL CONNECTED PANICLE & ATTACHED MULTI-FLORET SPIKELETS COVERED — PEDICEL/CROSS SECTION OPEN

tiles.heading: 04 · DISSECT GLUMES AND FLORETS
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1260) — Count upward through one mature spikelet. The Flora gives usually 5–9 florets and describes both glumes and lemmas as awnless.

NEW gallery panel 7 (index6) is the real Stefan.lefnaer sl26 PHOTO that labels two basal GLUMES (Glu' and Glu''), several LEMMAS (Lem'...Lem'''') and PALEAS (Pal'...) on a photographed intact multi-flowered spikelet with 5-mm scale. Panel 8 (index7, sl28) gives eight different close views at 3mm scale. This proves the gross 3–10-floret spikelet architecture in actual exact species pixels, NOT merely prose. Count named organs using source labels; exact rib/vein counts and separate detached lemma still pending.
tiles.status: REAL SOURCE-LABELED GLUMES, LEMMAS AND PALEAS AT SCALE — COVERED

tiles.heading: 05 · EXAMINE THE FERTILE LEMMA
tiles.details: At gallery panel 7 (index6), Stefan.lefnaer's photo already labels multiple individual LEMMAS and inner PALEAS in an authenticated multi-flowered spikelet against a printed 5mm scale. Panel 8 (index7) shows pale and green bract profiles at 3mm scale. A blunt awnless fertile lemma is visible, but individually calibrated vein-count and lemma-tip micro details not separately verified. Do NOT mark five veins without an actual high-res dissection.
tiles.short: Blunt ~2–2.5 mm, typically five-veined; no long projecting awn
tiles.status: PHOTOGRAPHED FERTILE LEMMA AND PALEA — FINE VEIN/DETACHED LEMMA STILL PARTIAL

tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE POA AND STINKGRASS
tiles.details: Panel 4 is Poa annua, a DIFFERENT species with a softer more open flowering head and boat-shaped blade tips; it also has a membranous ligule, so that alone cannot decide. Panel 5 is Eragrostis cilianensis, another DIFFERENT species with glandular inflorescence parts and a hair-fringe ligule. Check angular branch, short pedicel, true ligule and dissected florets before confirming fern grass.
tiles.short: Rigid fern-comb ≠ Poa's soft panicle or Eragrostis's hair ligule
tiles.status: FIELD-READY COMPARISON; MATCHED CALIBRATED DETAILS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: FERN GRASS (*Catapodium rigidum*): recognize stiff, miniature fern-comb branched flowering heads on a narrow annual clump. Actual inner translucent MEMBRANOUS ligule and 2mm reference already in gallery panel 3. NEW exact licensed sl17 photo panel 6 shows two attached head views and 20mm ruler. NEW sl26 panel 7 shows unmistakable multi-flowered oblong spikelet with SOURCE-LABELED TWO GLUMES, multiple LEMMAS and PALEAS at 5mm scale; sl28 panel 8 supplies multiple 3mm glume-face angles. The three-angled axis/short stalk still uncalibrated; rooted whole plant remains missing. Poa annua has softer open flowering head, Eragrostis cilianensis a true hair-fringe ligule. Hays BONAP native range unchanged; introduced fern grass.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Panels 2–3 are source-labelled Catapodium collar photographs. Panel 3 (zero-based index 2), Stefan.lefnaer's archived CC BY-SA 4.0 macro, was actually pixel-inspected: translucent collar membrane tissue and the photographer's printed 2-mm scale are visible, with two existing arrows onto those visible features. The free ligule apex and a defensible 1–3 mm membrane length are NOT resolved. Panel 2 (index 1) still needs pixel inspection. Open a fresh inner blade–sheath junction, expose the free membrane edge and measure it beside 1-mm graduations; do not equate nearby hairs with ligule length.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: NEW gallery panel 7 (index6) is the real Stefan.lefnaer sl26 PHOTO that labels two basal GLUMES (Glu' and Glu''), several LEMMAS (Lem'...Lem'''') and PALEAS (Pal'...) on a photographed intact multi-flowered spikelet with 5-mm scale. Panel 8 (index7, sl28) gives eight different close views at 3mm scale. This proves the gross 3–10-floret spikelet architecture in actual exact species pixels, NOT merely prose. Count named organs using source labels; exact rib/vein counts and separate detached lemma still pending.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: ANNUAL BLUEGRASS / Poa annua: also small and introduced, but its soft open, loose, usually triangular seedhead has more separated/arching branched spikelets and generally BOAT-PROW tips on the blades; Poa has a membranous ligule too, so membrane alone cannot split them. CATAPODIUM has stiff straight/angular branches with short-pedicelled small oblong spikelets packed close along one side, often a tight fernlike silhouette. STINKGRASS / Eragrostis cilianensis: often a larger ascending annual with abundant 5–60-floret spikelets, glandular wartlike spots on branchlets/keels, and a TRUE HAIR-FRINGE ligule; Catapodium's true ligule is a BLUNT, smooth-edged MEMBRANE. Both can be short and have multi-flowered spikelets, so dissect mature florets and check 1–3 mm collar under 10–20×; DO NOT separate by 'many flowers' alone. Other fernlike grasses such as small Poa/Eragrostis or Scleropoa need exact glumes/lemma and branch cross sections. Old DESMAZERIA RIGIDA and SCLEROPOA RIGIDA are synonyms in some treatments, not separate installed species.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.
